entries.group: L239 embedded-OSError rendering: `e.strerror or e` -> `e.strerror and e` changes which value is interpolated but still yields error text naming the fault; no reader depends on the specific rendering
entries.grounds: L239 branch; `{e.strerror or e}` becomes `{e.strerror and e}`. For the reachable OSErrors on this path (PermissionError/EACCES, IsADirectoryError/EISDIR from read_text), e.strerror is always a truthy string, so `or` yields strerror ('Permission denied') while `and` yields `e` i.e. str(e). Baseline why='RUN.json cannot be read (PermissionError: Permission denied) and aisef-run.jsonl is not there'; mutated why="RUN.json cannot be read (PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/.../RUN.json') and aisef-run.jsonl is not there" — observably different, but MORE informative (it now also prints the errno and the RUN.json path) and still names the fault and the artifact. Kill file 39 OK (SURVIVED): no test asserts the strerror-vs-str(e) rendering of this branch. Edge note: if an OSError on this path had e.strerror falsy (None/''), `and` would yield that falsy value ('None'/'' ) rather than str(e); such errors are not reached here (read_text's EACCES/EISDIR always populate strerror in CPython), and the overall detail stays non-empty via the surrounding literal. No consumer depends on which of strerror/str(e) is shown.
